summary: No region-specific signal was identified for Kahramanmaraş: the source inventory records no province-specific statute, incident, court decision or documented enforcement practice concerning trans people. The province stands under the national framework of Türkiye, under which national legislation such as the draft judicial package reported on 29 October 2025 extends to Kahramanmaraş without local modification, and the national assessment carried by the parent record applies to a trans visitor here.
tangentialFactors:
The incidents documented in the inventory fall outside this jurisdiction. The identity-check detentions of trans women on 31 July 2025 took place in Beyoğlu, Istanbul, where names were recorded and videos filmed; no comparable event in Kahramanmaraş appears in the sources, and the inventory contains no evidence that provincial police in Kahramanmaraş have carried out comparable stops.

The 2025 violation counts compiled by Kaos GL are national tallies drawn from media and civil-society reporting, because the state keeps no hate-crime statistics: six right-to-life violations of which three were recorded as hate-motivated killings with trans people most affected, 89 torture or ill-treatment violations against 51 the previous year, and 313 liberty violations at roughly 2.5 times the previous year. These figures carry no provincial breakdown and no population denominator, so they cannot be read as a ranking of provinces or as a measure of risk specific to Kahramanmaraş.

No source in the inventory compares provinces, and none ranks Turkish cities or regions by incidents affecting trans people, so no relative positioning of Kahramanmaraş against other provinces can be drawn.
localsOnly:
No resident-facing fact specific to Kahramanmaraş is recorded. The inventory contains no provincial police directive, no ruling of a Kahramanmaraş court, no provincial health-institution practice and no municipal facility rule bearing on trans residents, and it draws on no source local to the province such as provincial media, the provincial bar association or a local civil-society organisation.

Residents of the province stand under the same national framework as elsewhere in Türkiye, and the resident-facing picture, including detention conditions, healthcare access and the protection machinery available to them, is carried by the national record rather than by anything documented at provincial level.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the draft judicial package reported on 29 October 2025 has been enacted is unresolved in the sources; the inventory records the draft stage only and does not establish its subsequent status.

Whether Kahramanmaraş has province-specific enforcement practice is not sourced. No local source was consulted, so the absence of a recorded provincial incident reflects the scope of the inventory rather than a finding that trans visitors or residents face no exposure here.

The Beyoğlu detention account is out of scope for this jurisdiction and is carried only as context for what a visitor may encounter elsewhere in Türkiye.
